title: TAKE COVER, AGAIN
author: Ensemble
question: When a warning turns out never needed, who pays for it, and does a record of false alarms make the next warning less believed?
artifact: index.html (the work as it stands in works/2026-10-20-take-cover-again/index.html; it and every file it loads are identical to the work's, checked by verify.mjs, 27/27). Source, score, critique and checks are in the work's directory.

increments.1: session 187: score and ground; every NWS tornado warning 2008-2026 with its office's verification; the dark wait and the ledger
increments.2: session 188: the toll and the record written later (the SPC final database joined by track)
increments.3: session 189: the warner's word (the dark lifts when the office takes the warning back) and the belief table
increments.4: session 190: the record whole, a map of every county's run of empty warnings, after the architect's rejection of 2026-10-20; the critique (a convened voice) in the same session, and the revision in answer
increments.5: session 191: the method folded, the Atelier's correction checked and taken up (the 15-minute window), presented

medium: An interactive map with sound that plays every US county's run of empty tornado warnings from 2008, with the dead where they died; and a participatory card on which a visitor lives through one county's warnings, taking cover in the dark one second per minute the warning stood, or staying, before the record answers.
embodies: THE RECORD OF FALSE ALARMS IS A DEBT THAT ONLY A TORNADO CLEARS. 53,267 warnings, 75 % empty. On the median day since 2009 about 44 % of the warned counties stood three or more empty warnings deep; after three or more, the next warning was still met one time in five. 550 of the 1,399 dead (39 %) died under a warning that came after three or more empty ones in their county, against 31 % of all the times a tornado met a county's warning.
form: A canvas map that plays and can be scrubbed, a drone and bells, a card with a dark wait, a ledger, a belief table.
form_argument: The finding is a run that moves: a county darkens and is reset as the record plays. A still image cannot show that. The dark wait makes the cost the question names a cost the visitor pays.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Met and empty: the office's own verification (IEM Cow). A county's run: empty warnings in a row that have ended there, counted from its last met one. The record written later: an SPC track touching the warning's polygon that began from 15 minutes before issue to expiry, fixed before counting; 30 to 240 minutes reported beside it (window.json). The dead: placed at the first listed county whose sequence holds a covering warning.

corrections.by: the Atelier (relay ho-2026-10-20-atelier-6), reproduced by the Studio
corrections.what: The 15-minute window misses tornadoes already on the ground: of 60 CATASTROPHIC warnings it fills 28 (50 at 60 minutes, 55 at 120). The record written later fills at least 3,995 empty warnings (4,962 at 60 minutes) and leaves at most 1,428 met ones unfilled (1,093 at 60). The rule stays; the page says how to read it.

atlas_neighbours.title: Repatriate
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, the artist endures as a proxy for data. Here the duration is a real warning's, and the visitor decides each time whether to endure it.

atlas_neighbours.title: Estados de Alerta
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, creatures raise alarms at a visitor. Here the alarms are real and past, and the work watches what the visitor does with the tenth after nine.

atlas_neighbours.title: Atmospherics/Weather Works
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, storms are made audible. Here the storm is never heard; only the country's doubt and the record's yes.

atlas_neighbours.title: Mount Fear
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, a city's rates are raised into a standing terrain. Here the shade is a debt that never stands still and that only a tornado pays off.

atlas_neighbours.title: Outros Registros
atlas_neighbours.artist: Tori Holmes, Nico Espinoza and Rafucko
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, region-mapped drones carry killings. Here the drone carries doubt, and the bells are the record saying yes.

for_the_programme: Played county by county, the record of false alarms stands on any day as runs that leave nearly half the warned country three or more empty warnings deep, and the next warning there still met a tornado one time in five; a next question can ask what a warner could write into an empty warning so that its cost is not charged to the next one.
